question.text: Apart from the minimum sponsor commitment, what should the sponsor and fund manager list to evidence alignment of interests with LPs, per industry best practice in Ch 11.8?

answer.text: Other fund management activities carried out in a year, to indicate time dedicated to the fund, predecessor funds and establishing successor funds
All personal investments made by sponsor family offices over the past decade
Personal net worth of each KMP for the last 5 years
Capital gains tax paid by the sponsor in the preceding financial year

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.8 (Role of Human Capital), the sponsor/fund manager should list OTHER FUND MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES carried out in a year to indicate time dedication across current fund, predecessor funds, and establishing successor funds. This helps LPs assess whether the manager is spreading attention thin. The Trap: Personal investments, personal net worth, and personal tax returns are invasive and not industry-standard disclosures. Cross-Exam Context: Time-dedication disclosure tested in XIX-A (distributor) and XIX-C (manager-side PPM drafting). Manager's Pro-Tip: In the PPM, include an 'Other Activities' table with each KMP's hours per week across platforms. LPs calibrate their expectations — a CIO spending 30% on a successor fund is a yellow flag.
